claims.text: The threshold test runs on the GPS trace, not on the receipt's round number: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly bars trip_record.actual_distance_km from the threshold test. The trace records 22.40 km against the platform's own optimal of 17.60 km — an excess of 4.80 km, which is 27.3% of optimal and clears both the 20% test and the 0.80 km test — so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 carries admissibility weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and that its distance figure is the fact this claim rests on.

The 13 minute 30 second conflict between the trip record's started_at (18:32:10) and the trace's first movement (18:18:40) does not take the rider's case down, because the driver's own account supplies the explanation: he states the app kept showing the trip as not started. A meter that started late leaves the trip record's started_at as the erroneous field and the continuous, gap-free trace as the reliable one; the 2.38 km the trace records before 18:32:10 is therefore distance driven on this trip, not the tail of a previous job, and the 22.40 km figure is the one POL-RD-01 makes govern. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are both impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so its 22.40 km is not reduced. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap of more than 90 seconds, a fix-to-fix jump of more than 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds; EV-GPS-00112 has max_gap_sec 0.0, an empty gaps array, 100% coverage of the recorded window and a 10-second sample interval, so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires. Its 0.4 multiplier is a POL-GEN-02 confidence discount only, and the schema-IMPAIRED tag is not the same thing as policy impairment. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The driver's account that he made the Paya Lebar Quarter stop is contradicted by the trace, so it exonerates nothing. The chat log's waypoint_hint resolves the rider's request to a real venue coordinate (VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER), and the closest the vehicle ever comes to that waypoint is 512.35 m — far outside the 200 m corroboration test POL-RD-04 requires — so although the instruction was the rider's, was timely and named a specific place, the corroboration limb fails. Under POL-RD-14 an instruction the trace does not corroborate excludes no distance at all: POL-RD-04 does not apply, no part of the excess is written off as a rider-requested detour, and the deviation stands at the measured figure. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT; EV-CHAT-00112 is complete at weight 1.0.

Nothing on this record exonerates the excess as an external event. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching it and a route that leaves the optimal corridor before the segment and rejoins after; EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and its own issue detail records that no LTA advisory covers the PIE or the ECP in the 18:14–18:52 window, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and no amended optimal is supplied. Under POL-RD-08 the burden of naming a specific artifact and clause for any excuse sits with the driver, and an assertion that cites no evidence ID is discarded. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and that EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is a MISSING artifact cited for the absence itself.

No extra corroboration bar applies to this rider. POL-RD-08's rider-profile condition bites only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; the figures here are 1 and 0, so the claim needs no corroboration beyond the trace it is already measured on. Under POL-GEN-01 no other field on either profile — rating, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags or any other — may ground a finding about this trip, and the rider's case stands or falls on this trip's artifacts alone.

This case cannot be closed as NO_ACTION with the charge left standing on the rider. The pickup timestamps on two admitted artifacts — the trip record's started_at of 18:32:10 and the trace's first fix of 18:18:40 — disagree by 13 minutes 30 seconds, which is over the 10-minute limb of POL-RD-10(4); and independently the two artifacts that carry the excess, EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112, each sit at weight 0.4, so under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence in any ruling that rests on them is capped at 0.4, below the 0.70 floor that POL-RD-10(1) makes an escalation trigger. On either footing the disputed amount is held pending human review rather than collected from the rider. I disclose that both artifacts are impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

claims.text: The deviation the rider complains of is not established once the trace is measured across the recorded trip. The recorded events on EV-TRIP-00112 are a pickup at 18:32:10 and a dropoff at 18:52:20, and POL-RD-01 measures the actual distance as the length of the gps_trace polyline between those two events. EV-GPS-00112 carries 2.38 km of movement between its first fix at 18:18:40 and that 18:32:10 pickup, before this trip began. Measured across the recorded trip window the distance driven is 20.02 km against a 17.6 km optimal route, an excess of 2.42 km or 13.8 per cent, which fails the 20 per cent establishment gate and, no deviation existing, makes the outcome NO_ACTION. The fork is on the face of the bundle: the assessor's own note on EV-GPS-00112 records that the whole-trace reading gives 4.80 km and 27.3 per cent while the reading from started_at gives 2.42 km and 13.8 per cent, that this moves the measured excess across the POL-RD-01 threshold, and that nothing in the bundle decides which interpretation is correct. The rider carries the initial burden of the threshold showing under POL-RD-08, and an excess left unresolved between 13.8 and 27.3 per cent does not discharge it. I disclose that both artifacts I cite are impaired: EV-TRIP-00112 and EV-GPS-00112 each carry issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and a weight_multiplier of 0.4.

Even on the reading most favourable to the rider, where the whole 22.40 km trace governs and the deviation is established at 27.3 per cent, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic returns her nothing. The fare model is METERED, so recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 optimal km + 0.28 x 28.0 optimal minutes) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 optimal-route ERP + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 25.64. Charged_total is 25.26. The refund is charged_total less recomputed_fare, floored at zero: 25.26 - 25.64 = -0.38, so nil; and a nil refund is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, which POL-RD-02 makes NO_ACTION. The platform's own money block on EV-FARE-00112 says the same thing on its face: recomputed_fare 25.64, refund before rounding 0, quantum 0.05, payable 0.00. The rider was billed less on the distance and time lines than the optimal route would have cost her, so there is nothing on those lines to return.

This is not a MATERIAL deviation, so the rider's maximum remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial and never the uplift. POL-RD-01 makes a deviation material only where the excess exceeds 50 per cent of the optimal distance or 8.0 km absolute; the highest figure anywhere on this record is 4.80 km and 27.3 per cent, so neither limb is met, POL-RD-06 is not engaged on materiality, and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is open. If the profile is consulted anyway because the evidence is finely balanced, the pattern test fails on its own two fields: EV-DPROF-00112 records deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 296, a ratio of 0.003, below the 0.05 ratio POL-RD-06 sets and below the alternative count of 3. POL-GEN-01 confines that artifact to that test and no other field on it is cited here. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112, cited for the excess figures, carries issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and weight 0.4.

The trace is impaired at the schema layer and clean at the policy layer, and both statements must be made. The schema impairment is real and is disclosed: EV-GPS-00112 has status IMPAIRED, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and weight_multiplier 0.4, and it arises solely from its alignment with EV-TRIP-00112, not from any defect in the trace itself. The policy layer is clean, and the assessor says so on EV-GPS-00112: there is no gap (max_gap_sec 0.0, gaps empty), coverage_pct is 100.0 and the sampling interval is a steady 10.0 seconds, so none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires and the corroboration requirement and escalation consequences in POL-RD-10(3) are not triggered. Under POL-GEN-02 the down-weight caps confidence in whatever the ruling rests on, but it does not convert a policy-clean trace into one from which a deviation cannot be established, and the two findings must be stated side by side.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction available to the rider under POL-RD-09 to be added on top of anything. EV-FARE-00112 itemises erp_gantries as empty, tolls_erp at 0.00, airport_surcharge at 0.00 on a trip that neither originates at nor ends at an airport, and waiting_time_fee at 0.00. Its admissibility assessment records that the line items reconcile to the cent: 3.80 base fare + 15.00 distance + 5.66 time + 0.80 platform fee = 25.26. There is no off-route gantry and no phantom line, so no standalone pass-through refund and no billing-integrity finding arises.

In the alternative, on the reading that POL-RD-01's governing-field sentence prefers - the gps_trace figure governs the distance - the driver was under-billed rather than the rider overcharged. EV-FARE-00112 bills distance_charged_km of 20.00 while EV-GPS-00112 records trace_distance_km of 22.40, a shortfall of 2.40 km against the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04, so the driver is owed DRIVER_COMPENSATION at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 2.40 x 0.75 = SGD 1.80, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 and far inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is impaired, carrying issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and weight_multiplier 0.4; the billed-distance side of the comparison is carried by EV-FARE-00112 at full weight.

The rider's second complaint, that the Paya Lebar Quarter stop she asked for was not made, cannot found a refund on this fare. EV-FARE-00112 charges nothing for a stop and nothing for waiting: waiting_time_fee is 0.00, there are no fixed surcharges on the trip, and the platform fee is a flat 0.80; the only lines POL-RD-02 recomputes are the distance and time charges, and those are what the rider's own figures put in issue. She paid no charge for the stop she says she did not get, so that limb of the claim adds nothing to any amount the distance lines could produce.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute goes to a human reviewer and the disputed SGD 6.00 is held rather than collected or refunded (POL-RD-10; POL-GEN-03).

Why it cannot be finally decided. The two artifacts that measure this trip cannot agree when it began. EV-TRIP-00112 puts the pickup/start at 18:32:10; EV-GPS-00112 begins at 18:18:40 and covers 2.38 km before that moment. That is a 13 minute 30 second disagreement, beyond the 10-minute limb in POL-RD-10(4), and it decides the threshold test: read over the whole trace the trip is 22.40 km against a 17.6 km optimal, an excess of 4.80 km / 27.3% that clears POL-RD-01's 20% and 0.8 km gates and establishes a deviation; read from the recorded started_at only 20.02 km was driven, an excess of 2.42 km / 13.8% that fails them. The admissibility report itself records that nothing in the bundle decides which reading is correct. The driver's account that the app kept showing the trip as not started is an assertion that does not dissolve a contradiction the policy makes its own escalation ground, and on the other point he is contradicted by the trace.

Confidence. The deciding fact — the start-time conflict — is carried only by EV-TRIP-00112 and EV-GPS-00112, each rated weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, so under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence is capped at 0.4. That is below the 0.70 floor, which also triggers POL-RD-10(1) on its own. I record that this is schema-level impairment, not policy-level impairment: under POL-RD-07 the trace is clean (no gap over 90 s, no fix-to-fix jump over 500 m, a steady 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and I do not treat the trace as unusable for policy purposes.

For the reviewer, the arithmetic if a deviation is established. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 recomputes the optimal fare at 25.64 — (3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 km + 0.28 x 28.0 min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from EV-FARE-00112, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, surcharge or waiting charge — against the 25.26 charged, leaving a refund of nil, below the 0.50 de minimis. The driver's claim to SGD 1.80 for 2.40 unbilled km under POL-RD-04 rests on the same contested trace figure and likewise cannot be resolved here. There is no off-route ERP, toll, surcharge or phantom line to correct under POL-RD-09, and no POL-RD-06 referral: the deviation is not material (27.3% and 4.80 km are below the 50% and 8.0 km limbs) and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d of 1 against 296 completed trips establishes no pattern.

The Paya Lebar Quarter complaint adds nothing to any amount. The rider's request and the driver's 'ok can' are in EV-CHAT-00112, but the trace never comes within the 200 m corroboration test (nearest fix 512.35 m from the waypoint), so under POL-RD-14 the instruction is uncorroborated, excludes no distance, and no charge was levied for the stop in any event. No corroboration uplift applies to this rider under POL-RD-08 (deviation_claims_60d 1, substantiated 0), and no traffic advisory covers the trip window (EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0), so no external-cause exoneration arises.

What would resolve it on review: a record fixing when this trip truly started — a meter or booking log showing the meter start, or a GPS export placing the trace's first 2.38 km in a prior job — would let the excess be measured on a single window and end the dispute.

Both of you: this dispute cannot be decided on the present record, so it goes to a human reviewer. Under POL-RD-10 and POL-GEN-03 an escalation is terminal: the SGD 6.00 in dispute is held, not collected from the rider and not refunded to her, and no driver payment issues. POL-GEN-05 keeps the amount frozen while the review runs, and either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04 once the review decision issues. Two independent triggers fire.

TRIGGER 1 — POL-RD-10(4), timestamps disagree by more than 10 minutes. EV-TRIP-00112 records the pickup (started_at) at 18:32:10. EV-GPS-00112's first fix is 18:18:40 and it covers 2.38 km of movement before that time. Two admitted artifacts therefore disagree about when this trip began by 13 minutes 30 seconds, over the 10-minute limb, and the admissibility report on EV-TRIP-00112 flags exactly this as CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT citing POL-RD-10(4). The driver's account that the app 'kept showing the trip as not started' is an account of the conflict, not a resolution of it: it does not show whether the 18:18:40 tail belongs to this trip or to a previous job, and the pre-pass records that nothing in the bundle decides which reading is correct. A contradiction the policy names as its own escalation ground is not dissolved by an account from either side.

TRIGGER 2 — POL-RD-10(1), confidence below the 0.70 floor. Every distance figure this case turns on is carried by EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112, each at weight_multiplier 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT. Both are schema-IMPAIRED but policy-CLEAN: EV-GPS-00112 has max_gap_sec 0.0, an empty gaps array, 100% coverage and a steady 10-second interval, so no POL-RD-07(a)-(c) limb fires and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged — the two findings are stated side by side. EV-FARE-00112's distance_charged_km of 20.00 is the platform's own figure and, as its own assessment says, restates one side of the conflict rather than resolving it; the meter is derived from the same trace, so it does not lift the cap either. Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence is capped at 0.40, below the 0.70 floor POL-RD-10(1) makes an escalation trigger.

WHY THE UNDECIDED FACT MATTERS. If the whole 22.40 km trace is this trip, the excess is 4.80 km and 27.3% of the 17.60 km optimal (POL-RD-01's governing trace figure) and the deviation is established — but POL-RD-02 then returns nothing: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.60 + 0.28 x 28.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 25.64, which exceeds charged_total of 25.26; refund 25.26 - 25.64 is floored at zero and is below the 0.50 de minimis, so no refund to the rider. If the trip began at started_at 18:32:10, only 20.02 km was driven, the excess is 2.42 km and 13.8%, and no deviation is established at all. The driver's unbilled-distance claim (EV-FARE-00112 bills 20.00 km against EV-GPS-00112's 22.40 km = 2.40 km, which at 0.75/km would be 1.80, inside the 15.00 cap) turns on the same undecided fact. Each side's reading is genuine; neither can be fixed on this record, and the money outcome flips with it.

CLAIMS RESOLVED. Rider, POL-RD-14/POL-RD-04 (Paya Lebar Quarter stop): ACCEPTED — the chat log EV-CHAT-00112 (weight 1.0) shows the rider's instruction and the driver's 'ok can', but the nearest fix to the resolved waypoint VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER is 512.35 m, outside the 200 m corroboration test, so the instruction excludes no distance and any deviation stands as measured; it does not decide the case because the distance figures remain conflicted. Rider, POL-RD-10 escalation: ACCEPTED on the two triggers above. Rider, POL-RD-08 profile bar: ACCEPTED — deviation_claims_60d 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0, so no extra corroboration is required, and under POL-GEN-01 no other profile field may ground a finding about this trip. Driver, POL-RD-06 materiality and pattern: ACCEPTED — the highest excess anywhere is 4.80 km / 27.3%, below the 8.0 km and 50% material limbs, and on the citable fields only, EV-DPROF-00112's deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 296 is 0.003, below both the 0.05 ratio and the count of 3; no POL-RD-06(b) uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. Driver, POL-RD-09: ACCEPTED — EV-FARE-00112 shows no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge (the trip neither originates at nor ends at an airport) and no waiting fee, and the lines reconcile (3.80 + 15.00 + 5.66 + 0.80 = 25.26), so no standalone correction and no billing-integrity referral. Driver, the stop adds nothing on the fare: ACCEPTED — no fare line charges for a stop. Rider, that the driver's account resolves the conflict: REJECTED as a resolution, for the reasons under Trigger 1; the counterparty statement carries no weight and does not date the trip's start.

DISCARDED. The rider's claim that nothing exonerates the excess as an external event was discarded by the referee: it cited the MISSING artifact EV-ADVIS-00112-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) without naming its issue code, failing the POL-GEN-02(1) disclosure. The absence is noted — no LTA advisory covers the PIE or ECP in the 18:14-18:52 window — but it is not the deciding defect; the trace conflict is.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT. A record that dates this trip's start independently of the two conflicting artifacts — for example the driver device log for the preceding job, or a GPS export / meter or payment statement showing where the 18:18:40-18:32:10 tail belongs — and an independent statement of the distance actually driven.

The earlier route-deviation precedents P-0001 and P-0002 ended in PARTIAL_REFUND; this case differs because its distance figures straddle the POL-RD-01 threshold on two impaired instruments (0.4 each) that disagree about when the trip began, so the excess cannot be fixed well enough to rule on the money.

Both are schema-IMPAIRED but policy-CLEAN: EV-GPS-00112 has max_gap_sec 0.0, an empty gaps array, 100% coverage and a steady 10-second interval, so no POL-RD-07(a)-(c) limb fires and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged — the two findings are stated side by side. EV-FARE-00112's distance_charged_km of 20.00 is the platform's own figure and, as its own assessment says, restates one side of the conflict rather than resolving it; the meter is derived from the same trace, so it does not lift the cap either. Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence is capped at 0.40, below the 0.70 floor POL-RD-10(1) makes an escalation trigger.

WHY THE UNDECIDED FACT MATTERS. If the whole 22.40 km trace is this trip, the excess is 4.80 km and 27.3% of the 17.60 km optimal (POL-RD-01's governing trace figure) and the deviation is established — but POL-RD-02 then returns nothing: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.60 + 0.28 x 28.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 25.64, which exceeds charged_total of 25.26; refund 25.26 - 25.64 is floored at zero and is below the 0.50 de minimis, so no refund to the rider. If the trip began at started_at 18:32:10, only 20.02 km was driven, the excess is 2.42 km and 13.8%, and no deviation is established at all. The driver's unbilled-distance claim (EV-FARE-00112 bills 20.00 km against EV-GPS-00112's 22.40 km = 2.40 km, which at 0.75/km would be 1.80, inside the 15.00 cap) turns on the same undecided fact. Each side's reading is genuine; neither can be fixed on this record, and the money outcome flips with it.

CLAIMS RESOLVED. Rider, POL-RD-14/POL-RD-04 (Paya Lebar Quarter stop): ACCEPTED — the chat log EV-CHAT-00112 (weight 1.0) shows the rider's instruction and the driver's 'ok can', but the nearest fix to the resolved waypoint VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER is 512.35 m, outside the 200 m corroboration test, so the instruction excludes no distance and any deviation stands as measured; it does not decide the case because the distance figures remain conflicted. Rider, POL-RD-10 escalation: ACCEPTED on the two triggers above. Rider, POL-RD-08 profile bar: ACCEPTED — deviation_claims_60d 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0, so no extra corroboration is required, and under POL-GEN-01 no other profile field may ground a finding about this trip. Driver, POL-RD-06 materiality and pattern: ACCEPTED — the highest excess anywhere is 4.80 km / 27.3%, below the 8.0 km and 50% material limbs, and on the citable fields only, EV-DPROF-00112's deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 296 is 0.003, below both the 0.05 ratio and the count of 3; no POL-RD-06(b) uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. Driver, POL-RD-09: ACCEPTED — EV-FARE-00112 shows no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge (the trip neither originates at nor ends at an airport) and no waiting fee, and the lines reconcile (3.80 + 15.00 + 5.66 + 0.80 = 25.26), so no standalone correction and no billing-integrity referral. Driver, the stop adds nothing on the fare: ACCEPTED — no fare line charges for a stop. Rider, that the driver's account resolves the conflict: REJECTED as a resolution, for the reasons under Trigger 1; the counterparty statement carries no weight and does not date the trip's start.

DISCARDED. The rider's claim that nothing exonerates the excess as an external event was discarded by the referee: it cited the MISSING artifact EV-ADVIS-00112-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) without naming its issue code, failing the POL-GEN-02(1) disclosure. The absence is noted — no LTA advisory covers the PIE or ECP in the 18:14-18:52 window — but it is not the deciding defect; the trace conflict is.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT. A record that dates this trip's start independently of the two conflicting artifacts — for example the driver device log for the preceding job, or a GPS export / meter or payment statement showing where the 18:18:40-18:32:10 tail belongs — and an independent statement of the distance actually driven.

The earlier route-deviation precedents P-0001 and P-0002 ended in PARTIAL_REFUND; this case differs because its distance figures straddle the POL-RD-01 threshold on two impaired instruments (0.4 each) that disagree about when the trip began, so the excess cannot be fixed well enough to rule on the money."

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute is held for human review and no money moves today — the SGD 6.00 you contest, and the SGD 25.26 charged fare, stay where they are until a reviewer decides.

WHY IT CANNOT BE CLOSED ON THIS RECORD. The trip record and the GPS trace disagree about when this trip began, by more than the policy allows. EV-TRIP-00112 records the trip starting at 18:32:10; EV-GPS-00112 has the vehicle already moving at 18:18:40 with 2.38 km covered before that timestamp — 13 minutes 30 seconds, over the 10-minute limb of POL-RD-10(4). The disagreement is not cosmetic: measured over the whole trace the excess is 4.80 km, 27.3% of the 17.60 km optimal route, which would establish a deviation under POL-RD-01; measured only from 18:32:10 the distance is 20.02 km and the excess is 2.42 km, 13.8%, which would not. The driver's explanation — that the app kept showing the trip as not started — is an account of the conflict, and an account does not dissolve a contradiction the policy makes its own ground for escalation. That is the first trigger (POL-RD-10(4)).

SECOND TRIGGER, SAME FACTS. The confidence I may use is capped at 0.40. The artifacts that carry the distance and the fare recomputation are EV-GPS-00112 (trace 22.40 km; weight 0.40; issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT) and EV-TRIP-00112 (optimal 17.60 km and 28.0 minutes; weight 0.40; issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT). They are not independent of one another — both impairments arise from the same alignment conflict — so under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence must not exceed 0.40, below the 0.70 floor that POL-RD-10(1) enforces.

THE CLAIMS. Rider, POL-RD-01: I accept that the clause makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km govern, and the arithmetic is right (22.40 − 17.60 = 4.80 km, 27.3%, clearing both the 20% and 0.8 km tests), but that figure is carried only by artifacts at weight 0.40 and cannot be fixed at the confidence the floor requires. Driver, POL-RD-01/POL-RD-08: your competing measurement (20.02 km, excess 2.42 km, 13.8%) is the other side of the same unresolved conflict. Driver, POL-RD-02: your arithmetic is correct on its face — charged_total 25.26 against a recomputed_fare of 25.64 (base 3.80 + 0.75 × 17.60 km + 0.28 × 28.0 min = 24.84, plus the 0.80 platform fee; the surge multiplier of 1.0 was read from EV-FARE-00112), leaving a refund of nil and nothing above the 0.50 de minimis — so the rider recovers nothing on distance and time even if her deviation is accepted; but that recomputation takes its optimal distance and duration from EV-TRIP-00112 at weight 0.40, so it cannot be closed at the required confidence either. Driver, POL-RD-06: the highest excess anywhere on the record is 4.80 km and 27.3%, under both the 8.0 km and 50% limbs, so the deviation is not MATERIAL, and the pattern test fails on its own fields (deviation_flags_90d 1 against completed_trips_90d 296, ratio 0.003, below the 0.05 threshold and below the count of 3) — no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral issues. On both sides' trace-integrity arguments: EV-GPS-00112 is schema-IMPAIRED (weight 0.40, CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT) but clean for policy purposes (max_gap_sec 0.0 with an empty gaps array, 100% coverage, a steady 10-second interval), so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 do not fire and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. POL-RD-09: nothing to correct — erp_gantries empty, tolls and airport surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00, lines reconciling to 25.26 — so no pass-through refund and no billing-integrity referral. The Paya Lebar Quarter stop: the rider's request is in EV-CHAT-00112 at 18:33:02 and the driver agreed ('ok can'), but the closest the trace comes to the resolved waypoint is 512.35 m, outside POL-RD-04's 200 m test, so under POL-RD-14 the instruction is found, excludes no distance, and the driver's account that he made the stop is uncorroborated; in any event the fare charges nothing for a stop, so no refund turns on it. No traffic advisory is on file: EV-ADVIS-00112-01 is MISSING at weight 0.00 and no LTA advisory covers the PIE or ECP in the 18:14–18:52 window, so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing. Driver, POL-RD-04 compensation (billed 20.00 km against a 22.40 km trace, a 2.40 km shortfall, 2.40 × 0.75 = SGD 1.80): it cannot be granted here because it depends on the very trace figure whose alignment is unresolved. Rider, POL-RD-08/POL-GEN-01: accepted — deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0, so no extra corroboration bar applies, and no context-only profile field (rating, lifetime_trips, prior_deviation_flags) has been used as a ground; the referee's warnings on those mentions go no further.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT: a trip start consistent across EV-TRIP-00112 and EV-GPS-00112, or an independent record of the distance actually driven on this trip (a corrected trip record, a meter export, or an ERP gantry record), together with the routing engine's optimal-route record of 17.60 km and 28.0 minutes. Note for the reviewer: P-0001 and P-0002 share this case's clauses and were decided PARTIAL_REFUND, but neither presented two artifacts in cross-source conflict, at weight 0.40, carrying the distance figure.

To both of you: I cannot close this with a money ruling, so the SGD 6.00 in dispute is held for a human reviewer — neither collected from the rider nor refunded to her — and the driver is paid nothing now. The reason is the state of the two core instruments, not either party's account.

EV-GPS-00112 (GPS trace) and EV-TRIP-00112 (trip record) each carry status IMPAIRED, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and weight_multiplier 0.4. They disagree about when this trip began: the trip record's started_at is 18:32:10, while the trace's first fix is 18:18:40 and it records 2.38 km of movement before it — 13 minutes 30 seconds apart. That disagreement runs through the whole case. On the trace's governing figure (gps_trace.trace_distance_km 22.40 km, which POL-RD-01 makes govern) the excess over the optimal 17.60 km is 4.80 km, or 27.3%, so a deviation is established and is not MATERIAL (4.80 < 8.0 km; 27.3% < 50%). Measured only from started_at the distance is 20.02 km and the excess 2.42 km, or 13.8%, which fails the 20% test, and the bundle decides neither way. The trace is otherwise clean — max_gap_sec 0.0, no gaps, 100% coverage, 10-second sampling — so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) does not fire and the schema impairment is a POL-GEN-02 discount only; both statements are made. But the two artifacts that carry the excess both sit at 0.4, so under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence in any ruling resting on them is capped at 0.4, below the 0.70 floor, and POL-RD-10(1) requires escalation; the 13 min 30 s start-time conflict is over POL-RD-10(4)'s 10-minute limb as well. The driver's statement that the app 'kept showing the trip as not started' is noted, but an account (and a counterparty statement carries no weight) cannot dissolve an escalation ground the policy states.

The Paya Lebar Quarter request (POL-RD-04 / POL-RD-14): the chat log EV-CHAT-00112, at full weight, records the rider's request at 18:33:02 with a resolved waypoint and the driver's 'ok can' at 18:33:30, but the trace never comes within 200 m of that waypoint (closest fix 512.35 m). The instruction was the rider's, timely and specific, but the trace did not corroborate it, so it excludes no distance and the deviation stands as measured; the driver's assertion that he made the stop and waited is contradicted by the trace and carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

The money (POL-RD-02): even on the reading most favourable to the rider, the METERED fare gives her nothing. Charged_total was SGD 25.26, surge 1.0 (read from EV-FARE-00112). The recomputation is ((3.80 + 0.75 × 17.6 + 0.28 × 28.0) × 1.0) + 0.80 = SGD 25.64, so the refund is 25.26 − 25.64 = nil, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis. The driver's alternative claim to SGD 1.80 of unbilled-distance compensation (2.4 km × 0.75, the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04) is arithmetically right — billed 20.0 km against a trace of 22.4 km — but its entire premise is the same disputed 2.38 km, so it cannot be paid on this record and is one of the things the reviewer must settle.

POL-RD-06 gives no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral: the deviation is not material, and the pattern test fails on its own fields (deviation_flags_90d 1 against completed_trips_90d 296 = 0.003, below the 0.05 ratio and the count of 3). POL-RD-09 gives nothing — erp_gantries empty, tolls 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00 — so there is no phantom line to correct. POL-RD-08's extra corroboration bar does not apply to this rider (deviation_claims_60d 1, substantiated 0). No profile field decides anything here (POL-GEN-01); the context-only fields mentioned (rating, lifetime trips, prior deviation flags) were not used. Because no money moves, the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold is not engaged. This differs from the earlier partial-refund cases on these clauses because this fare was METERED and the optimal-route recomputation exceeds the sum charged.

What would resolve it: a record independent of the trace and trip record fixing the trip's start — a meter or app-start log, the platform's dispatch record for the preceding job, or a driver-device GPS export separating the 18:18:40–18:32:10 movement from this trip. With that, the reviewer can decide whether the excess is 27.3% or 13.8%, and whether the 2.4 km of unbilled distance is owed.

ledger.claim: The threshold test runs on the GPS trace, not on the receipt's round number: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly bars trip_record.actual_distance_km from the threshold test. The trace records 22.40 km against the platform's own optimal of 17.60 km — an excess of 4.80 km, which is 27.3% of optimal and clears both the 20% test and the 0.80 km test — so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 carries admissibility weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and that its distance figure is the fact this claim rests on.

The 13 minute 30 second conflict between the trip record's started_at (18:32:10) and the trace's first movement (18:18:40) does not take the rider's case down, because the driver's own account supplies the explanation: he states the app kept showing the trip as not started. A meter that started late leaves the trip record's started_at as the erroneous field and the continuous, gap-free trace as the reliable one; the 2.38 km the trace records before 18:32:10 is therefore distance driven on this trip, not the tail of a previous job, and the 22.40 km figure is the one POL-RD-01 makes govern. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are both impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so its 22.40 km is not reduced. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap of more than 90 seconds, a fix-to-fix jump of more than 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds; EV-GPS-00112 has max_gap_sec 0.0, an empty gaps array, 100% coverage of the recorded window and a 10-second sample interval, so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires. Its 0.4 multiplier is a POL-GEN-02 confidence discount only, and the schema-IMPAIRED tag is not the same thing as policy impairment. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The driver's account that he made the Paya Lebar Quarter stop is contradicted by the trace, so it exonerates nothing. The chat log's waypoint_hint resolves the rider's request to a real venue coordinate (VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER), and the closest the vehicle ever comes to that waypoint is 512.35 m — far outside the 200 m corroboration test POL-RD-04 requires — so although the instruction was the rider's, was timely and named a specific place, the corroboration limb fails. Under POL-RD-14 an instruction the trace does not corroborate excludes no distance at all: POL-RD-04 does not apply, no part of the excess is written off as a rider-requested detour, and the deviation stands at the measured figure. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT; EV-CHAT-00112 is complete at weight 1.0.

ledger.claim: This case cannot be closed as NO_ACTION with the charge left standing on the rider. The pickup timestamps on two admitted artifacts — the trip record's started_at of 18:32:10 and the trace's first fix of 18:18:40 — disagree by 13 minutes 30 seconds, which is over the 10-minute limb of POL-RD-10(4); and independently the two artifacts that carry the excess, EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112, each sit at weight 0.4, so under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence in any ruling that rests on them is capped at 0.4, below the 0.70 floor that POL-RD-10(1) makes an escalation trigger. On either footing the disputed amount is held pending human review rather than collected from the rider. I disclose that both artifacts are impaired at weight 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.

The deviation the rider complains of is not established once the trace is measured across the recorded trip. The recorded events on EV-TRIP-00112 are a pickup at 18:32:10 and a dropoff at 18:52:20, and POL-RD-01 measures the actual distance as the length of the gps_trace polyline between those two events. EV-GPS-00112 carries 2.38 km of movement between its first fix at 18:18:40 and that 18:32:10 pickup, before this trip began. Measured across the recorded trip window the distance driven is 20.02 km against a 17.6 km optimal route, an excess of 2.42 km or 13.8 per cent, which fails the 20 per cent establishment gate and, no deviation existing, makes the outcome NO_ACTION. The fork is on the face of the bundle: the assessor's own note on EV-GPS-00112 records that the whole-trace reading gives 4.80 km and 27.3 per cent while the reading from started_at gives 2.42 km and 13.8 per cent, that this moves the measured excess across the POL-RD-01 threshold, and that nothing in the bundle decides which interpretation is correct. The rider carries the initial burden of the threshold showing under POL-RD-08, and an excess left unresolved between 13.8 and 27.3 per cent does not discharge it. I disclose that both artifacts I cite are impaired: EV-TRIP-00112 and EV-GPS-00112 each carry issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and a weight_multiplier of 0.4.

Even on the reading most favourable to the rider, where the whole 22.40 km trace governs and the deviation is established at 27.3 per cent, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic returns her nothing. The fare model is METERED, so recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 optimal km + 0.28 x 28.0 optimal minutes) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 optimal-route ERP + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 25.64. Charged_total is 25.26. The refund is charged_total less recomputed_fare, floored at zero: 25.26 - 25.64 = -0.38, so nil; and a nil refund is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, which POL-RD-02 makes NO_ACTION. The platform's own money block on EV-FARE-00112 says the same thing on its face: recomputed_fare 25.64, refund before rounding 0, quantum 0.05, payable 0.00. The rider was billed less on the distance and time lines than the optimal route would have cost her, so there is nothing on those lines to return.

This is not a MATERIAL deviation, so the rider's maximum remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial and never the uplift. POL-RD-01 makes a deviation material only where the excess exceeds 50 per cent of the optimal distance or 8.0 km absolute; the highest figure anywhere on this record is 4.80 km and 27.3 per cent, so neither limb is met, POL-RD-06 is not engaged on materiality, and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is open. If the profile is consulted anyway because the evidence is finely balanced, the pattern test fails on its own two fields: EV-DPROF-00112 records deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 296, a ratio of 0.003, below the 0.05 ratio POL-RD-06 sets and below the alternative count of 3. POL-GEN-01 confines that artifact to that test and no other field on it is cited here. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112, cited for the excess figures, carries issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and weight 0.4.

The trace is impaired at the schema layer and clean at the policy layer, and both statements must be made. The schema impairment is real and is disclosed: EV-GPS-00112 has status IMPAIRED, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and weight_multiplier 0.4, and it arises solely from its alignment with EV-TRIP-00112, not from any defect in the trace itself. The policy layer is clean, and the assessor says so on EV-GPS-00112: there is no gap (max_gap_sec 0.0, gaps empty), coverage_pct is 100.0 and the sampling interval is a steady 10.0 seconds, so none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires and the corroboration requirement and escalation consequences in POL-RD-10(3) are not triggered. Under POL-GEN-02 the down-weight caps confidence in whatever the ruling rests on, but it does not convert a policy-clean trace into one from which a deviation cannot be established, and the two findings must be stated side by side.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity correction available to the rider under POL-RD-09 to be added on top of anything. EV-FARE-00112 itemises erp_gantries as empty, tolls_erp at 0.00, airport_surcharge at 0.00 on a trip that neither originates at nor ends at an airport, and waiting_time_fee at 0.00. Its admissibility assessment records that the line items reconcile to the cent: 3.80 base fare + 15.00 distance + 5.66 time + 0.80 platform fee = 25.26. There is no off-route gantry and no phantom line, so no standalone pass-through refund and no billing-integrity finding arises.

In the alternative, on the reading that POL-RD-01's governing-field sentence prefers - the gps_trace figure governs the distance - the driver was under-billed rather than the rider overcharged. EV-FARE-00112 bills distance_charged_km of 20.00 while EV-GPS-00112 records trace_distance_km of 22.40, a shortfall of 2.40 km against the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04, so the driver is owed DRIVER_COMPENSATION at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 2.40 x 0.75 = SGD 1.80, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 and far inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 is impaired, carrying issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT and weight_multiplier 0.4; the billed-distance side of the comparison is carried by EV-FARE-00112 at full weight.

The rider's second complaint, that the Paya Lebar Quarter stop she asked for was not made, cannot found a refund on this fare. EV-FARE-00112 charges nothing for a stop and nothing for waiting: waiting_time_fee is 0.00, there are no fixed surcharges on the trip, and the platform fee is a flat 0.80; the only lines POL-RD-02 recomputes are the distance and time charges, and those are what the rider's own figures put in issue. She paid no charge for the stop she says she did not get, so that limb of the claim adds nothing to any amount the distance lines could produce.
